subject: Re: Mid-cycle uplift — request for step-up credit rebalancing and co-term
messages:
From: Sarah Gomez <sarah@nimbushealth.com>
To: lauren_bishop@redwood.ai
Date: 2027-06-01T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Mid-cycle uplift — urgent: May spike and billing exposure

Hi Lauren,

Hope you’re well. We had a significant, unanticipated usage spike in May tied to a pilot that rolled out earlier than expected. The attached usage export shows a 4.2x increase week-over-week and we’re already tracking over our current committed bucket.

We’re committed to Redwood long-term and want to avoid disruption for our engineering teams. Two asks: can Redwood provide an interim credit to cover the May overage while we finalize a permanent uplift, and second, can we co-term the uplift to align with our existing Jan renewal so billing is simpler?

If helpful I attached the usage CSV and a one-page note from our Finance team. We’re hoping for a quick yes/no today so we can plan.

Thanks,
Sarah
Sarah Gomez
Head of Data & ML
Nimbus Health

Attachments: nimbus_usage_may2027.csv (csv), finance_note_may.pdf (pdf)
From: lauren_bishop@redwood.ai
To: Sarah Gomez <sarah@nimbushealth.com>
Cc: ben_carter@redwood.ai, priyom_das@redwood.ai
Date: 2027-06-01T10:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Mid-cycle uplift — urgent: May spike and billing exposure

Hi Sarah — thank you for the export and the clear ask. I’ve reviewed the CSV and looped in Ben (pricing lead) and Priyom (AM) so we can move quickly. Short answers up front: yes, we can propose an interim credit to amortize the May overage and we can co-term the uplift, but there are a couple practicals to agree on (effective date, lookback band, and whether you prefer a one-time credit or a staged voucher).

Proposed immediate steps:
- We’ll send a written interim credit proposal today to cover the May overage (one-time credit applied to June invoice) — Ben will draft.
- We’ll propose two co-term options: (A) Annualize the uplift now with a blended per-token rate and align to Jan 1 renewal; (B) Short-term uplift through Dec with a conversion credit at renewal.
- If you can confirm which option you prefer by EOD Tuesday we’ll prepare redlines and a DocuSign for signatures.

Ben / Priyom — please see attached usage and Sarah’s note. Ben, recommend a staged credit: 60% applied now, 40% held as a voucher against next quarter, so Nimbus has immediate relief but we preserve visibility into sustained consumption. Priyom, can you confirm the renewal date and any PO constraints?

Sarah — will aim to get the interim credit numbers to you within 3 hours.

Best,
Lauren Bishop
Director, Mid-Market Sales
Redwood Inference

Attachments referenced: nimbus_usage_may2027.csv
From: ben_carter@redwood.ai
To: lauren_bishop@redwood.ai, priyom_das@redwood.ai
Date: 2027-06-01T12:18:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Mid-cycle uplift — interim credit proposal draft

Lauren / Priyom — drafting numbers now. Key considerations I used: 1) May spike X tokens = ~1.45M extra tokens billed at list; 2) proposed interim credit = 75% of the overage value (covers runway but mitigates revenue risk); 3) for co-terming, recommend blended uplift rate that sits between current committed price and our standard uplift band — preserves org-level ARR uplift while keeping per-token economics palatable.

Two short asks for accuracy: Priyom, can you confirm NLU production start date (was it 2027-05-05?) and whether they already submitted a PO for the uplift? Also, does Finance at Redwood allow the 75% one-time credit or do we need approval from Sales Ops?

I’ll attach a redline for option A (annualize with blended rate) and option B (temporary uplift to Dec + conversion credit).

Cheers,
Ben Carter
Senior Sales Manager, Strategic Accounts
Redwood Inference

Attachments: proposed_co_term_redline.pdf
From: lauren_bishop@redwood.ai
To: Sarah Gomez <sarah@nimbushealth.com>
Cc: ben_carter@redwood.ai, priyom_das@redwood.ai
Date: 2027-06-04T15:48:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Mid-cycle uplift — interim credit and co-term plan

Hi Sarah — quick update and the plan we propose after internal review:

1) Interim credit: Redwood will apply a one-time credit equal to 70% of the May overage on the June invoice. We chose 70% as a compromise (Ben proposed 75% and Sales Ops countered at 65%). This is applied as a line-item credit and will clear immediately.

2) Co-term options (choose one):
  Option A (recommended): Annualize the uplift immediately. We’ll convert the uplift to a fixed committed band through Jan 1, 2028 with a blended per-token rate (we’ll include the numbers in the DocuSign). This gives you predictable monthly billing and higher committed volume discounts.
  Option B: Temporary uplift through Dec 31, 2027. If actual usage through Dec justifies it, we’ll convert remaining voucher value into the Jan renewal at a preferential credit conversion ratio.

3) Next steps: I’ve attached the redline (proposed_co_term_redline.pdf) and a one-page summary. If Option A works, reply with authorization and we’ll send the DocuSign today; if Option B, we’ll issue the interim credit now and prepare the temporary uplift amendment.

Priyom — please follow up on PO / procurement constraints and escalate to Sales Ops if they need the 75% number approved.

Sarah — please let us know which option you prefer by EOD Monday and we’ll finalize paperwork. Appreciate your promptness here — want to keep your teams uninterrupted.

Best regards,
Lauren Bishop
Director, Mid-Market Sales
Redwood Inference

Attachments: proposed_co_term_redline.pdf, interim_credit_summary.pdf
